players.reasoning: route developing
CB is ahead and ready; I start with a fake to draw their hips, then will snap to the 40° break once I see commitment to the fake.
WR is behind with small lateral gap. Keep eyes on WR while retreating to maintain distance; WR has FULL burst available, so backpedal to mirror and avoid over-committing.
route developing

Executing the planned fake to 40° to threaten the CB and cause a commit; now accelerating toward top speed to maximize separation once CB reacts. No call yet since final cut not completed and CB not yet committed.
WR still upfield with full burst; no 2+ step heading change yet. Maintain backpedal to mirror and watch, close depth gradually instead of fast cuts.
route developing
continue stem to sell fake; wait for CB to commit and then snap break
WR is not yet committed; maintain backpedal with small lateral mirroring toward WR's projected spot (stay between WR and center field).
route developing
continue selling the fake on the stem heading; wait for CB to commit to a hip turn and for rec>0 before snapping the break
WR showing full burst but has not committed to a real cut; maintain backpedal to watch and mirror lateral movement, gradually closing the projected angle without committing to a large cut
route developing
Continue stem fake; CB not committed yet (rec=0). Plan to snap to break on next step once CB rec>0

WR committed to a real cut (40°) and is slow relative to projection; switch from backpedal to normal and close on the WR's projected catch angle toward 0.5s ahead (119° bearing). Aim to intercept rather than maintain backpedal defense.
WR has not called for the ball yet; wait for the WR to signal and for the route to develop before targeting a projected open spot.
CB heading committed to fake; rec>0 window open. Burst to break now for separation and ball catch timing
Maintain current pursuit with no hard cuts. WR has full burst available, and I am in recovery (1 rec). Continue toward WR's projected path and wait for burst to clear before making a decisive cut.
WR has not called for the ball yet and the route is developing; wait for the call to avoid a broken play.
CB rec=0; CB ahead by y but not committed yet. Begin speed fake to force a misread, then burst to break with separation. Maintain break heading 40° to stay in route timing.
WR has held a real cut (40°) for 2+ steps; switch to normal and close on intercept angle toward WR's projected position (bearing 83°).
WR has not called for the ball yet; wait for the cut/opening around t≈2.3s to exploit the projected window while the CB is still in recovery.

CB rec=1 indicates a partial commitment; still close but a burst could create separation. Since break is in progress and we’re already heading 40°, accelerating now maximizes glide past the CB if they hesitate or fail to fully recover. Don’t call until we have clearer separation and the CB is clearly behind or off our break path.
WR has held a 40° cut for 2+ steps (confirmed real cut). Switch to normal mode and close on an intercept angle toward WR's projected position. Focus on contesting the ball and reducing separation.
WR has not called for the ball; wait for the upcoming cut to develop the window.
CB rec>0 and heading is committing; continue bloom to top speed while maintaining the stem to force CB to choose
Mirror minor WR adjustment: WR has started a mild lateral move (0.1s step to 40°); shift ~+10° toward projected position to maintain cushions without triggering cut recovery.
WR has not called for the ball; wait for his release and the projected open window around t≈2.0s before throwing.

We are on the break heading but CB hasn’t committed (rec=0). Maintain the existing break while edging toward top speed to threaten a quick burst once CB hesitates or commits. Waiting for CB to turn will create the window for a clean separation before we call for the ball.
WR held 40° heading for 2+ steps (real cut). Switch to normal and angle toward WR's projected position to contest.
WR has not signaled for the ball yet; the route is still developing toward the t≈2.0–2.3s cut, so waiting prevents a mis-timed throw.
CB heading rose to 62°, rec=1; ready to snap into break on next step when they commit
WR held a real cut to 40°; switch to normal and close on an intercept angle toward their 0.5s projected position
WR has not signaled for the ball yet; wait for the planned cut around t≈2.0–2.3s to see if separation opens before the sack clock tightens.
Sell fake with stem at 40°; wait for CB commit (rec>0) before final cut to 90°-break for separation

WR is within close proximity with FULL burst available. Make a small 6-10° inward adjustment toward WR's projected path (toward 51° bearing) to tighten cushion and stay between WR and ball without triggering a cut Recovery.
Waiting for WR to call for the ball; his cut around t≈2.0s will open a window, and we must avoid throwing before the call.
CB rec likely >0 next step and heading shifting confirms commitment; keep current break heading and conserve speed for a sharp snap on the real break to maximize separation
Mirror minor WR movement toward projected position (49°). WR has full burst potential but no confirmed cut yet; maintain close, patient alignment and reduce angle error toward the catch zone.
WR has not called for the ball yet; window likely develops around t≈2.0–2.3s, so hold to let the cut establish.
Holding current stem toward 40° to set up CB commit. CB not yet recing; will snap to break next step per plan.
WR shows no real cut; maintain close mirror to projected position (47°) and stay between WR and target, ready to contest if ball arrives
Waiting for WR to call; the route will develop around t=2.0–2.3s, so throw only after the WR signals to maximize window and avoid sack.
CB rec is 0 and heading hasn't committed yet. Maintain stem and accelerate toward top speed to threaten the break and set up the next window when CB commits.
WR has FULL burst; maintain close mirror toward their projected path (0.5s ahead) while preserving spacing. Small heading adjustment toward 50° to contest without over-committing.
WR has not called for the ball yet; the route cut is expected around 2.3s, so hold to wait for the signal.
CB rec=0; no commit yet. braking now can close gap and set up a clean burst into the 40° break once CB hesitates, maintaining the planned break direction
WR has been holding a 40° heading for 2+ steps (real cut). Switch to normal and angle toward the WR's 0.5s projection to pursue an intercept.
WR has not called for the ball yet; I’ll wait for the signal to avoid throwing into an uncertain window before the cut at ~t=2.0–2.3s.
CB rec is 0 and CB is not committed yet; prepare to explode into the 40° break once CB commits or at the planned break time
WR has held a real cut (40°) for 2+ steps; switch to normal and close toward the intercept angle (approx 44°) to contest the pass.
WR is about to call for the ball; wait for the call and the window to develop before throwing.
We are at break heading already but separation is minimal (CB very close). I’ll push toward top speed to maximize speed on the break and watch CB rec; only call when CB is behind or gap grows.
WR shows slight lateral drift; mirror toward projected position (43°) while awaiting real cut
WR has not called for the ball yet; wait for the anticipated cut around t=2.0–2.3s to align with the projected open spot.
Slip is staged; CB not committed to fake; continue stem toward break direction to threaten separation and watch CB rec for a commit to snap on next step
WR is in a controlled two-way move with full burst; mirror and close slightly toward projected WR position (42° bearing) to maintain near man coverage without committing to a large cut.
Waiting for WR to call for the ball; the route cut around t≈2.3s will open a window as he breaks and CB is in play, so hold until the signal.
CB not committed; can't call yet. Push for better separation while maintaining break direction
WR has held a 40° heading for multiple steps; confirmed real cut. Switch to normal and close on intercept angle toward WR projected pos (24.9,60.7) in 0.5s.
WR has not called for the ball yet; wait for the call as the route develops and the WR may break around t≈2.3s.
Window available as CB is committed to my fake; explode off real break to maximize separation
WR just committed to a real cut toward 40°, projected to (25.5,61.4); switch to normal and close on intercept angle toward their projected position.
WR is about to signal and the window will open after the cut; throwing now risks incomplete or contested catch.
CB rec>0 and heading committed to my fake; break alignment 40°; I am open on the break and ready for ball.
WR maintains 40° diagonal; mirror with small 0° change, stay in phase and ready to close if he commits
CB is in full burst and closing quickly; current separation is only 0.6 yd, so the window will likely close before the ball arrives—wait for a clearer open window.
Ball is in air to your current heading; no further deception. Maintain separation and adjust only by acceleration to maximize catch probability. Facing 40° aligns with ball path for easier catch.
WR is within close range and not committed to a real cut yet; maintain mirror, stay patient, ready to contest if ball is thrown.

Ball is in the air to the current heading. Do not alter route; facing-adjust toward landing for easier catch while maintaining separation.
WR drifting upfield-right with small lateral movement; mirror toward WR's projected position (45°) to maintain close press without committing; no real cut yet
CB and WR are very close with tight 0.69 yd separation; wait for a clearer window as WR continues toward 62.6 y and CB may close
QB threw to your heading; must stay on path to catch. Increase speed to ensure catch as CB tight though. Facing toward ball landing aligns catch window.
WR is trimming to upfield-right with full burst; mirror their diagonal path and maintain proximity to contest the catch

WR has held a new heading (40°) for multiple steps; real cut confirmed. Close on intercept angle toward their projected 0.5s position (38° bearing).
Window is tight with both players in full bursts; CB will close further before arrival, wait for clearer separation.

QB threw to where you would be if you held 40°. You should not change heading now; you’re in a good path to catch. Boost to max speed to minimize CB closing distance, and orient your eyes toward the ball's landing zone (≈40°) to maximize catch likelihood.
WR has held a 40° heading for 2+ steps (real cut). Switch to normal and close on intercept angle toward WR's projected position (bearing ~38°).

WR showing no real cut yet; mirror slightly toward their projected position to stay between them and the catch zone while waiting for commitment

Deception no longer needed; separation achieved. Hold heading to align with throw trajectory and maximize catch probability.
Ball in air; WR is 0.6 yd lateral from me and moving; mirror toward the projected zone (39°) while keeping eyes on WR at 33° to contest the ball.
ball in air
QB threw to projected spot; maintain heading, set facing to 185 as instructed to catch; no need to change path since ball is coming from QB toward you and you are at target landing zone
Ball in air: align toward landing zone (38°) and contest with swat; WR has full burst but close proximity allows a swat if timed to ball path.
ball in air

The ball is in air toward your projected spot. Do not change heading; keep 40° to ride your break into the landing zone. Set facing to 186 to align eyes with the ball's approach. Use accelerate to reach the landing zone (about 0.12s ball travel, 0.8 yd gap to zone).
Ball in air; aim at landing zone (39°) and face/point toward it to swat. WR is in FULL burst but ball ETA ~0.12s; close to zone center, use swat with arm at 1.0 yd reach.

Facing 188 keeps eyes toward the QB, while the ball arrives. No need to call again; you already signaled earlier and must hold heading until catch.
Ball arriving; align to landing zone and attempt swat since within reach and angle favorable.
